prize_parts.citation: for the prediction of flat electronic bands in twisted bilayer graphene at a magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in moire flat bands

statement.case_for: I have moved from B034 to B013. In round 1 I rested my first choice on conceptual originality and the cleanliness of a two-name credit. Having read all eight statements, the weight of the objections to B034 is not something I can answer on the science. Six colleagues independently say that the experimental realisation of the Cirac-Zoller programme was already honoured in 2012 and, through the entanglement work, in 2022, and that a theory-only prize would honour the blueprint without the demonstrations. I still think proposals and experiments are distinct contributions, but I cannot show that a narrow citation separates them cleanly, and I should not hold B034 to a lower standard than I would hold B061 on overlap. B013 is the strongest case on the criterion that the chair's questions bring out. A quantitative prediction (Bistritzer and MacDonald, 2011) of flat bands at a specific twist angle was followed by an experiment (Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators, 2018) in which nature delivered gate-tunable correlated insulators and superconductivity in a carbon-only system. The result has been reproduced by many independent groups and extended to other moire platforms. As a theorist I find the prediction-then-observation structure the most convincing evidence that the physics is understood at the level that matters. If the criterion is novelty of the regime opened, B013 leads. If it is completeness of the claim, B061 leads. I weigh the first more heavily here, because the existence and reproducibility of the platform do not depend on the unresolved pairing mechanism.
statement.case_against: The credit is the real weakness. Yuan Cao and Valla Fatemi, first authors of the 2018 experiments, as well as Dean, Young and Ashoori on the related moire work and the earlier band-structure theorists (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto), fall outside a three-name limit. I do not have a principled rule that makes this painless. The most defensible reading is that Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive prediction and that Jarillo-Herrero's group led the decisive experimental programme, but I would want the omissions stated in the record and not hidden. The pairing mechanism and the nature of several correlated states are still unsettled, and eight years is short next to the decades behind B061. If the committee concludes that the field is still moving too fast to fix a citation, B061 is the more finished alternative and I would not object to it.

responses.point: Kroll argues that B034 is better after the experimental record matures, that a prize for the theory risks reading as a verdict in an open competition between platforms including circuit QED, and that B061 is the cleanest answer to what can be measured and how accurately.
responses.response: His platform-competition point is fair and I accept it. I work in circuit QED and would be uneasy if my own preference for B034 looked like a verdict on platforms, so it is a further reason I step back from it. On B061, I accept that the lattice clock is a different physical idea from the 2005 comb and the 2012 single-ion control, and I withdraw my round-1 suggestion that the clock is as exposed to the overlap objection as B034. Where I still differ is the criterion. A tenfold gain in precision on an existing quantity, however well measured, is a different kind of result from a new regime of correlated matter. I place B061 as my first alternative, not the lead.

responses.point: Lindroth says the lattice clock is a different platform and physical idea from the 2012 work, that B034 is not separable from what was recognised in 2012 and is a fallback rather than a lead, and that B013 is the stronger candidate if the committee wants a prize that opens a new field.
responses.response: Her distinction between a new field of physics and a new level of measurement is the criterion the chair asks us to make explicit, and by that criterion I land on B013. I concede her point on B034: the demonstrated payoff came through experimental groups that fall outside a Cirac-Zoller pair. I also take her atomic-structure case for B061 seriously, since the magic wavelength and blackbody shift are calculable and the physics is under control. That makes B061 a safe outcome, but I read the regime-opening criterion as the one the prize is for. I would not call a B061 outcome a mistake.

responses.point: Mehlig ranked Cirac-Zoller sixth because the proposals are partly recognised via 2012 and 2022, the citation must choose between ion gates and cold-atom simulation, and a theory-only prize sits less comfortably with a discovery that nature delivered. He also opposes dropping Bistritzer from B013.
responses.response: I agree on both points. The scope question I listed myself in round 1 does not go away, and I now think it counts against B034 more than I allowed. On Bistritzer, I agree that dropping him severs the 2011 prediction, which is the part a theorist can say with confidence is the origin of the whole programme. I would keep all three names rather than a two-name MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero pair, unless the committee finds a principled reason to treat the two parts asymmetrically.

responses.point: Eriksson says the Cirac-Zoller proposals are original and well confirmed, but the experimental realisations (Wineland, Blatt) are largely outside the credited pair, whereas B013 has theory and experiment together in one set, and that Cao's exclusion is a real gap the shortlist cannot fix.
responses.response: I accept his objection to B034 and it is a main reason I changed. On Cao, we agree it is a real gap. I would not use that gap to defer B013. A three-name limit forces any prize in a large field to leave people out, and the clock candidate has the same issue with Lemonde, Takamoto and Ludlow. I would support his request that the omissions be stated openly in the record, so that the three names are read as the decisive prediction and the decisive experimental programme, not as a claim that no one else mattered.

responses.point: Danielsson weights breadth of new physics and says B013 is robust across specialisms, with the unresolved superconducting mechanism treated as follow-on physics.
responses.response: I agree with his reading of maturity. The flat bands, the correlated insulators and the reproducibility across groups and platforms are established regardless of how the pairing mechanism is eventually resolved, so the mechanism bears on citation wording and not on validity. That is why I keep the citation to the flat-band prediction and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, with no claim about the origin of the pairing. I do not rely on his count that four members rank B013 in their top two, since support counts should not substitute for judgement. My agreement rests on the reproduced physics.

responses.point: Olsson moved to B061 as a concrete, quantitatively controlled invention, but notes that B013 has stronger breadth of impact and equal first-place support, and asks whether the 10^-18 milestones belong to Ye alone or to a wider group.
responses.response: Her measurement-based argument is strong and I treat B061 as the best alternative. Her question about the 10^-18 milestones is also a real attribution risk that I find harder to settle than B013's, because lattice-clock results are spread over several laboratories and I cannot say from the supplied evidence which of them a two-name credit would leave out. I note that she herself concedes B013's breadth of impact. That is the point on which I weigh the two candidates differently from her.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can adopt a principled rule for omitting Cao, Fatemi and others from B013. I think the decisive prediction plus the decisive experimental programme is defensible, but I cannot show it is the only reading.
Whether the unsettled pairing mechanism is a timing reason to wait. I judge it is not, since the platform is reproduced, but the interpretation of several correlated states is still moving.
Whether B061 should be preferred if the committee wants the most complete, longest-confirmed claim, and whether other lattice-clock groups have claims that a Katori-Ye credit omits.
I am relying on my own recollection of the history and attribution and have not verified it independently.
statement.conflict_note: My disclosure is unchanged. I have documented professional links to Chalmers colleagues Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson and to my frequent co-author Anton Frisk Kockum, and I direct WACQT, which works on superconducting circuits and quantum computing. These bear most directly on B018 (circuit QED), where I would recuse myself from the discussion, and I have not proposed it. Chalmers also hosted researchers associated with the 2025 prize. I have no documented tie to the credited names in B013, B061 or B034. I note that B034 lies close to my own field of quantum-computing theory, which is a further reason for caution in advocating it.
